doc.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Carole King and Lou Adler as friends; the takes and Tapestry
summary: He describes King and Adler, the double solos kept on separate tracks, and how Adler persuaded King to record Tapestry.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Yes. They both were there. Let me just say at the outset they have remained to this day dear friends, they are both wonderful people. I actually did a podcast with Lou recently. I wanted to do one with Carole King but one of her daughters who is her manager, I called her and she said, “Listen, Tom, I don’t think — the answer will be no I can tell you now. She just doesn’t want to dwell on the past anymore.” You know she’s probably done a billion interviews and you know there’s a point at which you go enough already. So, and

plus she always lived a rather solitary life. She was in Idaho in a very, very remote part of Idaho. I’m not even sure they had indoor plumbing. It was really, really, you know in the woods kind of lifestyle. And just what a great lady. Lights up a room every time. So anyway, so I listened to the thing, they say play what you feel, I go out and I started playing. And I did a couple of takes but I just, I don’t know we connected. I connected with this tune. And I did maybe two or three takes. They — actually they kept all of them and there’s a couple of spots where you can hear me playing like two different solos simultaneously. Because they just — I don’t know they liked the sound of the two things I played.
That was on purpose then, not like bleed over from —

No, no, no, not at all. Because they were all on separate tracks so there was no bleed at all. So that went well. That was a delightful session and you know with Carole King she had just come off the incredible success of “Tapestry” the album she did for Lou. In fact Lou was the one who said to her, “You know Carole, you ought to consider not just doing demos for other people but do your own record.” And she was, you know maybe. He talked her into it and the result is “Tapestry.”
